title: Reduce kernel churn by adding stochastic backoff and telemetry gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a high-concurrency capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed sustained oscillation in runtime kernel selection resulting in elevated p95/p99 tail latencies and increased token cost. The immediate root causes were: (1) aggressive scheduler probing that amplified transient score differences between quantized and fused attention kernels, (2) noisy telemetry spikes (KV cache misses, microbatch rejections) that were being consumed raw by the kernel scorer, and (3) an attention autotiling heuristic that reacted to short-lived sequence-length spikes.

Goal:
Reduce kernel-selection churn and stabilize latency/cost without regressing median latency or throughput. Primary mechanisms: introduce a probabilistic (stochastic) backoff to dampen probe frequency per-worker, and add telemetry gating + smoothing before signals are used by the kernel scoring model.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Stochastic backoff per-execution-path: each worker maintains a lightweight moving window for recent kernel-switch attempts. When a probe triggers, instead of always attempting a kernel switch immediately, the worker will flip a biased coin whose probability decays with the number of recent switches. Backoff parameters are tunable by route/model. This reduces synchronized probing waves and gives KV cache/attn autotile time to stabilize.
2) Telemetry gating and exponential smoothing: raw signals (cache miss rate, microbatch rejection, seq-length histogram delta) will pass a gate that requires sustained deviation for T seconds (configurable) OR a smoothed metric threshold to be crossed before affecting kernel scores.
3) Scoped feature flags and rollout knobs: implement flags at route and model version granularity. Provide canary percentages and a kill-switch in the console for immediate rollback.
4) Safety fallbacks: if backoff reduces throughput below threshold, automatically relax backoff; if tail latency increases, revert to last-stable kernel policy.

Acceptance criteria:
- kernel-switch-rate (per-worker) p95 drops by >=40% during synthetic burst tests that previously reproduced the incident.
- p99 request latency does not increase by more than 5% during normal loads.
- token cost per request remains within 3% of baseline for stable workloads.
- No increase in cache-miss sustained rates after rollout.
- Feature flags allow fast rollback and metric-driven canary progression.

Action items and owners:
- Design backoff algorithm and parameter defaults (Miguel) -- prototype ready by 2026-03-08.
- Implement per-worker backoff state and coin flip logic (runtime) (Sana Iqbal) -- PR and bench by 2026-03-12.
- Implement telemetry gating + smoothing pipeline change (observability infra) (Ethan Lee) -- gating config and tests by 2026-03-10.
- Add control-plane feature flag and console toggles (Console) (Priya Menon) -- UI + API by 2026-03-15.
- Create synthetic stressbench scenario that reproduces wave behavior (Benchmarks) (Jorge Ramos) -- harness by 2026-03-05.
- Define canary rollout plan and playbook (Ops/Oncall) (Aisha Patel) -- plan by 2026-03-09.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overly aggressive backoff may increase median latency under certain steady-state workloads. Mitigation: tune backoff floor and use throughput-sensing relaxations.
- Telemetry gating adds detection latency; rare transient regressions may take longer to correct. Mitigation: short initial gate with direct kill-switch.
- Added complexity in scoring pipeline requires ops runbook updates and observability surfaces.

Telemetry and dashboards to add:
- kernel-switch-rate (per-path and per-worker) p50/p95/p99
- gated-signal-delay (time between raw deviation and gated signal) distribution
- per-route canary percent and health check metrics (latency, throughput, cost)
- rollback latency (time from detection to rollback event)

Rollout plan:
1) Internal bench + unit tests (benching harness) -> measure baseline.
2) Nightly integration build with flags enabled but default off for 24h.
3) Canary to 1% of production traffic for models with heavy throughput for 2 hours, monitor metrics and escalation runbook.
4) Ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with artifacted blast radius and rollback on threshold violations.

Longer-term follow-ups (post-ship):
- Investigate learning-based probe scheduling (deferred).
- Model-driven scoring with explicit uncertainty estimates so telemetry gating can use confidence bands.

This ticket contains the detailed implementation plan for the backoff and gating features; separate follow-up tickets will track canary execution, runbook updates, and post-rollout analysis.
